subject: gk
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution restricts and prohibits religious instructions in the educational institutions which are maintained by the Government and funded by the government ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 28** of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
 
• It allows religious instruction only in institutions established and maintained by religious denominations or trusts with prior consent.
 
• Under Article 28(3), attendance at religious instruction or worship in institutions recognized by the state cannot be made compulsory.
 
• This Article ensures the secular character of state-funded institutions and safeguards individual freedom of religion.
 
• It is a vital provision to maintain the principle of secularism, as enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism in India:**

 
 
• India follows a unique model of secularism where the state maintains an equal distance from all religions.
 
• It ensures freedom of religion under Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 25:** Guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 26:** Provides the right to manage religious affairs, including establishing and maintaining institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
 
• **Article 27:** Prohibits the state from compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:** The Supreme Court of India has emphasized that secularism is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution, as highlighted in the S.R. Bommai case (1994).
